title: Loongson 2K1000 AHCI write and durability validation
summary: Add bounded polling WRITE DMA EXT and FLUSH CACHE EXT support to the existing 2K1000 AHCI transport, connect ext4 BlockImage barriers to the block device, establish failure-only diagnostics and host regressions, then admit real-board media writes only through explicit safety gates.

in: the existing one-slot polling AHCI transport and its private 4 KiB bounce buffer
LBA48 WRITE DMA EXT data-out commands and FLUSH CACHE EXT non-data commands
direction-correct command-header, PRDT, DMA cache, publication, completion, and timeout behavior
first-failure-only AHCI runtime diagnostics suitable for serial capture
host command-layout, bridge, error, and regression tests
LA64 2K1000 compile/build admission before any real-board reset request
staged read-only, disposable-media, persistence, filesystem-check, and workload real-board experiments
out: LA QEMU Pmap, IPI, or TLB protocol changes
repeating CPU-pin, stack, fairness, or hardware-fact investigations already closed at 42cd4396
AHCI interrupts, NCQ, multi-slot scheduling, direct caller-frame DMA, hotplug, port multipliers, or recovery reset machinery
changing the RV64 VF2 MMC implementation or treating its no-op barrier as a durability model
raw writes to guessed free LBAs, partition-table edits, mkfs, resizing, or destructive fsck
modifying local-images/alpine-linux-loongarch64-ext4fs.img or creating a replacement root image
writing the onboard competition disk before explicit user approval of the exact filesystem-level probe
rebasing or merging the updated main branch during this implementation slice

write_sets.notes: One local implementation lane. Existing board HAL resource facts, DMA mapping policy, QEMU TLB code, the Alpine mother image, and the real disk remain outside the write set. Ext4 error-type edits are admitted only if the phase-3 red test proves the bridge otherwise destroys EROFS/EIO identity.

steps.title: Freeze the implementation and media-safety experiment contract
steps.notes: The protocol names hypotheses, canonical gates, red tests, expected register/DMA behavior, stop conditions, rollback, and the explicit approval boundary before any board-media write. A repository-wide progress/docs failure is recorded with exact pre-existing findings rather than hidden.

steps.title: Add host regressions for AHCI write and non-data command layout
steps.notes: The tests must first fail because 0x35, 0xEA, the W flag, and non-data command preparation do not exist. READ DMA EXT layout remains a locked control.

steps.title: Implement bounded WRITE DMA EXT through the existing bounce workspace
steps.notes: Retain one slot, polling, 32-bit constrained DMA and one page per command. Copy source Frame to bounce, sync bounce ToDevice, set command-header W, publish before PxCI, wait for completion/error, and require PRDBC=4096. Keep empty, overflow, capacity, frame-mapping, kernel-overlap, and 48-bit-LBA checks explicit. Do not add NCQ or direct Frame DMA.

steps.title: Implement FLUSH CACHE EXT and connect the ext4 BlockImage barrier
steps.notes: FLUSH CACHE EXT uses a register H2D FIS with PRDTL=0 and W=0, no bounce sync, and a flush-specific deadline long enough for ATA cache drain. BlockDeviceImage must override BlockImage::barrier and drive BlockDeviceOps::barrier. Preserve EROFS/EIO if a small format-error extension is required; never continue collapsing all transport failures into Truncated/EINVAL.

steps.title: Add first-failure-only AHCI runtime observation
steps.notes: Record cumulative failure count plus the first operation/LBA/error/PxIS/PxTFD/PxSERR/PxCI snapshot. Emit at most one compact serial record per boot and nothing per successful command. Expected input/range errors do not count as transport failures.

steps.title: Run host, formatting, boundary, and LA64 build admission
steps.notes: No reset request and no image deployment before all changed-path focused gates and the physical-target build pass. Pre-existing unrelated workspace failures are preserved verbatim and separated from changed-path regressions.

steps.title: Boot the new driver read-only and prove no read-path regression
verification: Real board boots with tx.root=sda ro, identifies 62533296x512, mounts ext4, enters Alpine shell, and reads known files.
The boot boundary contains no AHCI runtime-failure record, CPU-pin/stack/cmdline failure, panic, or unexpected disk-write witness.
steps.notes: This is the first point at which Codex asks the user to reset. The board remains read-only; no media mutation is authorized by this phase. Codex operates the serial bridge and debugging; the user only resets when requested.

steps.title: Run a filesystem-level write, barrier, persistence, and offline-check probe on approved disposable media
verification: On a user-approved clone/spare medium, create one uniquely named file, write a deterministic 4 KiB pattern, fsync, rename, fsync the directory, read and hash it, delete it, fsync again, and observe no AHCI error.
After power-cycle, the expected durable state is present and an offline e2fsck -f -n reports no new error.
steps.notes: Never probe a guessed raw LBA. If no disposable clone/spare medium exists, stop after the read-only control and ask for explicit approval before substituting the onboard filesystem. Do not modify the local Alpine mother image.

steps.title: Accept the onboard ext4 filesystem only after disposable-media closure and explicit approval
verification: Repeat the bounded file/fsync/rename/power-cycle check in a dedicated /root/tx-ahci-write-probe directory on the explicitly approved onboard filesystem.
Persist resolver and CA/config changes through ordinary filesystem calls; never disable TLS verification.
Run bounded Git init/add/commit, clone/post-clone, sustained TLS requests, shell responsiveness, host ping, and final filesystem-check acceptance with no AHCI or kernel invariant failure.
steps.notes: The user owns reset and media approval; Codex owns commands, serial capture, diagnosis, and stop/go decisions. date -u changes realtime state but is not itself a filesystem persistence test.

steps.title: Record evidence, close the implementation slice, and commit only scoped files
steps.notes: Host implementation may be committed before hardware mutation. Keep real-board phases pending until their exact evidence exists; do not mark the whole plan complete merely because code builds. Do not add a coauthor.

verification.notes: The new record parses with jq, but repository-wide validation stops at the untouched docs/progress/plans/2026-07-24-network-time-integration.json because it uses step status completed instead of complete.
The repository reports the same existing 31 broken links and 6 stale-vocabulary warnings. Neither new experiment file appears in the findings.
The changed tx-ext4 lane passes 39/39 and tx-scripts passes 167/167, but the repository gate remains red in the existing tx-shims dispatch group and two tx-kernel libctest command assertions.
19/19 AHCI tests passed, including write/flush layout, LBA48 range, progressing/stalled clock behavior, and first-failure observation. Full tx-drivers is 43/43.
7/7 bridge tests passed, including the red-to-green barrier delegation counter, retry mapping, and EROFS/EIO fidelity. Full tx-fs is 106/106.
The physical target completed full-build: ok. --no-image deliberately avoided rebuilding or replacing the Alpine root image.

verification.command: cargo test -p tx-ext4-format && cargo test -p tx-ext4 --lib
verification.notes: tx-ext4-format passed 51 unit/integration tests including journal and recovery coverage; tx-ext4 passed 39/39 including ReadOnly/Io errno mapping.
Formatting and whitespace checks passed after the implementation edits.

risks: Setting ATA opcode 0x35 without AHCI Command Header W=1 reverses the HBA transfer interpretation and is a hard stop covered by host layout tests.
Using FromDevice cache synchronization for the write bounce buffer may send stale data on non-coherent LA64; command planning and implementation must use ToDevice.
Returning success from BlockImage::barrier without delegating to BlockDeviceOps violates ext4 journal ordering even when the SATA driver has a correct flush command.
A total polling-iteration cap can expire far earlier than the ATA flush time on a fast CPU; the wall-clock deadline and stalled-clock escape must be distinct.

After a TFES, interface, host-bus, or timeout error, blindly issuing another command may reuse an unsafe port state. The first implementation fails closed for the current request and reports the register snapshot; automatic port recovery remains out of scope.

The onboard SATA filesystem is the competition environment and currently has no declared disposable clone. Raw-LBA experiments or early writable boot could corrupt it; the plan requires read-only control and explicit media approval.

The existing bridge collapses all block errors to Truncated/EINVAL. Without narrow error fidelity or a first-failure driver record, real-board diagnosis would misclassify transport errors as ext4 format failures.
Existing active progress records contain a legacy completed step status and broad overlapping scopes, so repository-wide progress validation may remain red independently of this new record.
blockers: Real-board write phases require the user to identify or approve the exact disposable/competition medium and reset when requested.
Offline e2fsck requires the tested filesystem not to be mounted and an available trusted fsck environment; if unavailable, hardware acceptance stops before original-media promotion.
